searchText: On MEV-Boost at merge: Currently many parties across the eco-system, from r/ethstaker to staking pools are gearing up for the merge and deciding whether to implement/guide users to use MEV-Boost. While the small delay at the merge before MEV-Boost is activated is certainly helpful, there is still a large risk to block production post-merge if much of the network activates MEV-Boost and there is a problem. I am writing this to ask the EF (e.g. <@552133098075193354>) and CL teams to consider putting out guidance on whether they suggest that users activate MEV-Boost prior to/at the merge, or if it would be better for the network to phase in MEV-Boost usage over time after the merge is complete and the MEV-Boost flow has had time to demonstrate its stability. Without any such guidance I fear that many users will assume that MEV-Boost has been tested/engineered to the same standards as the rest of the merge infrastructure, which I do not believe to be the case. One issue is that some staking pools already have MEV. You'd be giving the big guys a big advantage over pools like rocketpool at merge as they could offer much higher rewards. As well, if mev-boost doesn't exist, we are back to gas wars over MEV If the relay doesn't offer a block, or one that pays well, then the local EL produces one. And if we don't trust that relays can verify valid blocks, then that also means the EL used in the relay can't verify valid blocks and we have a bigger problem than mev-boost Last thought: Not even sure how this would work. "Please make less on your block proposals, just in case there's an issue with mev-boost. Yeah you. You should make less. I'll be "phasing in" mev-boost on my proposals in the meantime". Is that the message? I'd say the key message is that people need to understand they are trusting the relay and should monitor to make sure it really is working properly. The automated fallback handles most cases but can't help with a relay that fails to reveal the payload after the block header is signed. And you always to make sure the produced block really did pay you the tx fees it promised. Agreed Trust but verify Now doing that manually may be a little tricky if there's no log for how much the block promised to pay. Does Teku spit that out? I'm not familiar with the details but I don't think Teku even knows what the block was supposed to pay. The relay is responsible for selecting which block provider to use. er relay might the wrong term actually - the sidecar process (mev-boost being the only one currently I think) I think it’s more just acknowledging that mev-boost is essentially in beta so take that into account when deciding to activate it before it’s been seen to work well in the real world. The delta in rewards for waiting a week or so will be negligible. Some staking pools have in-house mev solutions. Mev-boost is for the smaller pools and solo validators to prevent all validators gravitating towards 1-2 entitites. Impossible to verify perfectly if its anything like pow. Time lags between places really affect it. It's simple to verify. You check that your fee recipient balance increased by the amount the builder promised it would after processing the block. Whether they paid you for every cent of mev included isn't important - just that they paid what they offered. In an ideal world if what is offered is less than what your local EL would have earned then you'd pick the block from your local EL but I don't think there's any support for that currently (the engine API doesn't currently include information how much the local block would earn the fee recipient) Ah you meant if the builder paid you the amount. I thought you meant if the builder choose the maximum value. Since the builder can pull an EDEN and maximize their own value. I would expect that builders are paying as little to validators as possible. It's why you want to have multiple builders and then you pick the one that pays the most. ie competition will force them to pay the validator more and keep less for themselves. Makes sense, sorry for being so uninformed. Oh interesting wrinkle, I didn't know that. How did Bellatrix go on Prater? last I checked, it seemed about 5% of the network did not upgrade otherwise, good/stable In the Prater Becan Chain explorer https://prater.beaconcha.in/ Why are there no Epochs listed after epoch 112,262. (while block proposal are appearing for later Epochs) ? Beaconcha.in having issues. They'll sort it soon hopefully. tks amazing imposter Oh was wondering. Thought it’s just a discord bug. 🐼 While I do think MEV-Boost is unfortunate, I acknowledge it is the best/only fleshed out mitigation for the MEV issue. I'm just concerned about the short-term reliability/performance of it surrounding its initial activation. CL teams hands are tied by the risks to client diversity in terms of forcing a significant delay post-merge prior to activation. excerpts.content:
On MEV-Boost at merge: 

Currently many parties across the eco-system, from r/ethstaker to staking pools are gearing up for the merge and deciding whether to implement/guide users to use MEV-Boost.

While the small delay at the merge before MEV-Boost is activated is certainly helpful,  there is still a large risk to block production post-merge if much of the network activates MEV-Boost and there is a problem.

I am writing this to ask the EF (e.g. <@552133098075193354>) and CL teams to consider putting out guidance on whether they suggest  that users activate MEV-Boost prior to/at the merge, or if it would be better for the network to phase in MEV-Boost usage over time after the merge is complete and the MEV-Boost flow has had time to demonstrate its stability.  

Without any such guidance I fear that many users will assume that MEV-Boost has been tested/engineered to the same standards as the rest of the merge infrastructure, which I do not believe to be the case.

And you always to make sure the produced block really did pay you the tx fees it promised.

excerpts.content: While I do think MEV-Boost is unfortunate, I acknowledge it is the best/only fleshed out mitigation for the MEV issue.  I'm just concerned about the short-term reliability/performance of it surrounding its initial activation.
